detail.abstract: Essential services are often regulated by quantity: a minimum level (a floor) is guaranteed in kind, and consumption above it may be capped or charged. This paper studies such rules in a general-equilibrium economy in which the service is supplied under decreasing returns, so that its price rises with demand and the sector earns rents, the floor is procured in the same market, and the authority that runs the service observes consumption but not income. Curbing consumption above the floor then lowers the service price, transferring income from the recipients of service-sector rents to purchasers and to those who finance the floor. Whether this price channel raises welfare depends on who bears the cost of the floor and who receives the rents. A pure ceiling acts only through this channel and can raise welfare under lump-sum financing; in the numerical illustration, no binding ceiling raises welfare under proportional financing with rents attributed in proportion to labor income. A charge on consumption above a threshold, the dual of a constraint on upper-tail dispersion, adds redistribution through an equal rebate. The optimal constant rate is the sum of a distributional term and a price term determined by the supply elasticity, the incidence of the floor's cost, and the attribution of rents. Even when the schedule may be any function of consumption, the price channel leaves a component of the marginal charge common to everyone, which under lump-sum financing reflects only differences in rent shares. Numerically, the charges raise welfare under both forms of financing; under lump-sum financing, the constant-rate charge outperforms the welfare-optimal ceiling and attains most of the gain of the optimal such schedule. When labor income is observed and taxed by an optimal nonlinear income tax, the part of the price channel that runs through the cost of the floor vanishes, while the part that runs through unobserved rents remains.

detail.abstract: In trade execution, traders are concerned with market impact, how far their own trading moves the price. Typically this is measured using a dataset of the slippages of previous orders, however these are noisy as most price changes are not related to a trader's previous activity. We study refined slippage: benchmarking orders against a counterfactual price implied by untraded, correlated peer assets. The resulting estimator of impact model parameters can shrink standard errors substantially and is unbiased unless there is cross-impact, which attenuates all parameters by a common factor. We use this estimator to derive a Hausman specification test for the presence of cross-impact. We additionally model the maximum size of cross-impact that is compatible with the absence of arbitrage and use this to derive expressions indicating the maximum potential bias of refined slippage for each set of peer assets chosen. In this we find choosing peers substantially more liquid than the traded asset results in low potential bias, indicating refined slippage is safe to use in these circumstances.

detail.abstract:
This paper studies the relationships between State financing, money creation, the foreign exchange market and consumer prices in Zaire, and then in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, from 1980 to 2010. It extends the historical study of Congolese inflation over 1909–1980. The analysis combines 31 annual observations with 78 monthly observations on Kinshasa prices, the parallel dollar rate and currency outside banks between January 1990 and June 1996. Over the whole period, for a given change in the exchange rate and past inflation, 10 additional log points of M1 growth are associated with 7.75 additional log points of inflation. During hyperinflation, the clearest monthly relationship concerns the parallel dollar rate: a 10-log-point rise in that rate is associated with a 6.99-log-point rise in Kinshasa prices in the same month.

An increase in net bank claims on the State equal to one point of GDP is associated with 17 additional log points of M1 growth; this relationship becomes less precise when 1990–1996 is excluded. The 2001 stabilisation, based on exchange rate unification, floating and cash-management discipline, brought average monthly inflation down from 18% to 0.71% within a few months and lowered median end-year inflation to 15.8% over 2002–2010, despite a rise to 53.4% in 2009 that was quickly reversed in 2010. Finally, over sixteen one-year-ahead forecasts, adding the lagged exchange rate and M1 to an inflation equation does no better than carrying forward the last observed inflation. The variables that make it possible to follow a crisis as it unfolds thus have more limited power to forecast its turning points, which argues for a regularly updated assessment of monetary and fiscal conditions.

detail.abstract: In large common-value uniform-price auctions with finitely many states and signals, partially revealing prices make bidders tie at the clearing price. Existence of equilibrium then has two components: price feasibility, governed by restrictions shared by all rules that ration only tied bids, and rationing implementation by the auction's own rule. Both can fail robustly. With two signals and three states, an equilibrium generically exists if and only if the informationally intermediate state does not have the lowest value. With three signals, there is an open set of economies on which the pro-rata auction has no equilibrium but rationing by announced signals, an endogenous type-dependent sharing rule, restores one: there, an anonymous rule cannot divide the surplus of a tie between two marginal types with different information. With two signals, no alternative rule that rations only tied bids restores an equilibrium that is absent under pro rata. Under pro rata, existence at a candidate price function is a linear system plus one product condition per pooling price, and reduces to linear programming when pools are thin.

detail.abstract: Organizations rely on expert advice even when neither investigation nor accuracy is verifiable. We show that higher-order uncertainty about experts' incentives need not increase the minimum expected payment for information. With two experts, any equilibrium implementation can be made robust at arbitrarily small additional expected cost, even when experts care about the decision or investigate only intermittently. For experts who care only about compensation, we derive the exact cost of every randomized decision rule. For state-dependent decisions, the bound is approached by concentrating investigation on the lower-cost expert and using occasional independent verification. The cost separates information production from the rents needed to motivate it: a decision's state-independent component reduces investigation but does not eliminate those rents. Limited contingent payment capacity constrains the savings from infrequent checks. The results distinguish the cost of organizing expertise from the cost of sustaining its incentives.

detail.abstract: Smart-contract audits are the main assurance device in decentralized finance, however research has measured only whether a protocol was audited and by whom. We build a dataset of 509 public audit contests from Code4rena and Sherlock (2021-2025) with 9,449 High and Medium findings, sponsor responses and reviewer overlap, and link 334 audits by hand to 181 DefiLlama protocol families. We find that a protocol's own audit had flagged the vulnerability class of its later exploit in 56.7% of 30 cases, against 43.8% for audits of comparable protocols. Second, more High-severity findings are associated with lower total value locked (TVL) 26 weeks after launch and with lower TVL before the audit existed. Third, depositors do not act on audit content. After 208 large exploits, protocols with a disclosed weakness of the same class lose no TVL relative to other audited protocols, and effects beyond 5% are rejected. Protocols differ in quality, and depositors observe much of that difference through channels other than the audit, such as the team, the design, and earlier products. The High-severity count is a usable screen for protocol quality. The classes flagged in a protocol's audits show where it is likely to fail even after fixes, and risk pricing should rest on what an audit found and not on whether one exists.

detail.abstract: Do financial markets, maritime supply chains, and war-risk insurance markets register preparations for armed conflict before diplomatic warnings and public reporting peak? Existing scholarship relies primarily on single-asset event studies or news-based geopolitical indices that rise once media attention intensifies. This article develops the concept of anticipatory decoupling: the observable reallocation, withdrawal, or repricing of assets, shipping routes, liquidity, and contractual claims when strategic actors and market intermediaries anticipate coercion or armed conflict across exposed international networks. The theory specifies three dimensions that govern the observability and direction of pre-onset anomalies: structural position within global financial and logistical hierarchies, network dependence on third-party clearing and transport infrastructure, and the anticipated strategic end-state of conflict. Coding 28 armed conflicts (1950–2026) alongside 12 non-war crisis placebos under an onset-date-blind protocol (κ = 0.893 for timing; κ = 0.890 for confounds; Online Appendix Table A.1) identifies pre-onset anomalies in eleven cases. In our mixed-methods design, a nested three-tier historical audit (N = 11 pre-onset cases, N = 5 unconfounded cases, and N = 3 declassified archival cases: Lebanon 1975, Iran–Iraq 1980, and Yugoslavia 1991, alongside two provisional 2025–2026 applications and six closed-channel “hard cases” that validate theoretical scope boundaries) traces microfoundational mechanisms, while population base rates and out-of-sample generalization are estimated on a two-tier panel (1946–2026 country-months, N = 6,144; 2010–2026 country-weeks, N = 4,240). Rare-event logits (including a pre-2025 historical subsample, PR-AUC = 0.685), multi-country within-state war-versus-sanctions Difference-in-Differences (G = 8 states, 16 windows, exact randomization-inference p = 0.0003), and Jordà local projections show that calibrated cross-domain alerts outperform single-domain models out of sample (PR-AUC = 0.790 rolling-origin; 0.603 LOCO; 0.578 Leave-One-Country-Out) and complement diplomatic and structural benchmarks within a hybrid multi-sensor ensemble (PR-AUC = 0.903 rolling-origin; 0.615 LOCO).

detail.abstract: This study examines the determinants and income effects of e-commerce adoption among rural employers and employees in Indonesia, with a focus on both agricultural and non-agricultural sectors. Using nationally representative labor force data from 2018 to 2024, we estimated probit models to analyze adoption patterns and applied ordinary least squares (OLS), propensity score matching (PSM), and quantile regression to assess the income impacts. Results show that education, training, gender, and sectoral affiliation have a significant influence on adoption. Notably, adoption remains lower among agricultural workers and women. E-commerce adoption is associated with substantial income gains across all groups, particularly among agricultural employers, who earn over 44 percent more than non-adopters. Employees also benefit, though to a lesser extent. Quantile regression results indicate that lower-income workers gain the most, suggesting e-commerce can reduce rural income inequality. However, Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition reveals persistent gender earnings gaps, with adoption alone insufficient to eliminate disparities. These findings underscore the necessity for inclusive digital strategies that extend beyond infrastructure, emphasizing digital literacy, targeted training, and gender-sensitive policies to foster equitable rural development.

detail.abstract: On 3 October 2013 an Associated Aviation Embraer 120 crashed shortly after takeoff from Lagos, killing sixteen of the twenty people on board. The family of one of the passengers sued the airline and the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority. The Federal High Court held both liable. The Court of Appeal set aside the judgment against the Authority. It reasoned that the claim was governed exclusively by the Montreal Convention, as applied to domestic carriage by section 48(2) of the Civil Aviation Act 2006, and that the Authority, not being the carrier, could not be liable. The negligence findings against the Authority were declared otiose. This article argues that the decision was wrong. The exclusivity rule in the Convention, and in the statute that applies it to domestic flights, is defined by its subject matter and by its defendant. It governs actions against the carrier, its servants and its agents. It says nothing about the liability of a regulator. That the Authority was not the carrier placed it outside the Convention. It did not place it beyond the reach of the law. The correct question was whether the Authority owed the passengers a duty of care under Nigerian law and breached it. That question was never decided. The article then examines the Civil Aviation Act 2022, which shortens the period for suing the Authority to three months and provides that no action shall lie for its decisions on safety. It argues that the new provision must be read narrowly, so as to protect the regulator's choices of policy but not its negligent performance of operational tasks. Read in that way, the regulator answers to the travelling public for operational failure, but not to the operator it regulates, and not for policy.

detail.abstract: Mobile financial services (MFS) can increase access in Bangladesh, but also provide quick and cheap routes for money mules and freezing accounts leaves customers with limited options. We ask the questions: Does a structural signal help predicting mule status? Does a heterogeneous graph attention network (HAN) provide additional out-of-time value over gradient-boosted trees (GBT)? Can ant colony search (ACS) be an alternative to exact temporal cycle enumeration at lower cost, producing the same or similar results? What is the cost of a false-freeze cap in terms of recall? We simulate a Bangladeshi MFS network consisting of 269,170 wallet-weeks (7,500 wallets, 119 mules in 28 planted rings) for 36 weeks, score only wallets that haven't been flagged, use the same tuning budget for all models and run 10 seeds with wild-bootstrap inference. The HAN outperformed XGBoost on wallet attributes (PR-AUC 0.668 vs. 0.610) but not significantly (after Holm correction), and was comparable to XGBoost with neighbourhood aggregates (0.664-0.668). Across 22 further generated panels the HAN beat XGBoost on controls every time (mean +0.147) but not the aggregated XGBoost (mean-0.008, and-0.037 with the signals). The specified ant colony achieved a 59% recall on 72 independent graphs, a 90% recall cost more than a pruned exact search, and pheromone learning did not help. A single conservative threshold was as effective as a rural threshold in controlling the false freezes in rural areas, while a rural threshold was holding false freezes to 1.76% at a 1.5 point cost of recall. Results are description of planted structure, rather than actual mule behavior.

detail.abstract: Language models are now a standard tool for measuring what managers say on earnings calls, but the encoders behind these measures were usually pretrained on text from the same years a backtest covers. Holding out a test period does not remove that hindsight, because it sits in the features. We adapt NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, to earnings calls without letting it read anything dated after 31 December 2023. The calls supply the training signal themselves: every analyst question is followed by management's answer, and the model learns to pick that answer out from the other answers of the same call. We test on every US call from January 2025 to October 2026 (20,323 calls, 254,575 questions) and make every modeling choice on calls from 2024. The adapted model, NoLBERT-Calls-2023, ranks the true answer first for 78.0% of questions (95% interval 77.8-78.2; chance 8.0%), against 26.3% before adaptation. It is 1.0 point ahead of a call-adapted ChronoBERT, 3.4 points ahead of a call-adapted FinBERT, and 18.7 and 19.8 points ahead of the best off-the-shelf retriever and BM25. A year-by-year test over 2013-2026 finds no look-ahead premium: relative to a model adapted only through 2012, the released model does no better on the years it was trained on than on years it never saw. The price of the cutoff is compute: under one shared 150-minute recipe NoLBERT adapts least well of four encoders, and its lead comes from a longer, staged adaptation of about 13 GPU-hours.

detail.abstract: This paper examines legal encryptions generated by capitalism to manage 'workers'. Our focus is on how urban governance systems in capitalist mode encode exploitation and exclusion into legal and bureaucratic frameworks. Taking the case of Bangalore (magnet of software industry in the globe) to show how capitalism organizes life and death for waste workers. By interrogating the intersection of caste, labor, and infrastructural governance, the study explores how the persistence of manual scavenging and hazardous sewer work reflects structural inequalities embedded in urban modernity. While technological discourses promise hygienic cities and smart infrastructures, the everyday reality of sewage management relies on the embodied labor of marginalized caste communities, exposing them to toxic environments and premature death. Drawing on Achille Mbembe's concept of necropolitics, the paper argues that the sewage system operates as a space where sovereignty is exercised through disposability-where certain bodies are sacrificed to sustain the metabolism of capitalist urban life. Short span of life of sewage workers is a manufactured reality that is preconditioned for quality of life through a capitalistic logic of production of time. Through an analysis of fact-finding reports on deaths of sewage workers, policy documents, court judgments, post-mortem reports and trans-disciplinary accounts, the paper reveals how state and market logics produce a regime that naturalizes death as an occupational hazard rather than a political failure. This study highlights the ethical and political imperative to rethink infrastructural justice beyond technocratic solutions, foregrounding the lived experiences of those who clean the detritus of capitalist growth.

detail.abstract:
This working paper traces the evolution of monetary regimes in the Congo between 1909 and 1980. Drawing on monetary conventions, the reports of the issuing institutions and banking and macroeconomic statistics, it identifies seven historical configurations. For each, the analysis establishes who held the power of issue, which reference set the external value of the currency and on what terms agents could obtain foreign exchange. Two decisions structure the last decade studied. In March 1976, the authorities replaced the parity of two dollars per zaire with a peg to the special drawing right. In November 1978, they began revising this parity in steps.

Between 1968–1975 and 1976–1980, average end-of-year inflation rose from 20.36% to 69.16%. Over the same periods, net bank claims on the State rose from 14.06% to 25.68% of GDP, a difference of 11.62 points. The corresponding difference for credit to firms and households is 2.59 points of GDP, with a 95% confidence interval that includes zero. These results describe the monetary and fiscal conditions under which Zaire changed its anchor. The brevity of the series, concurrent external shocks and the adjustments begun as early as 1978 limit the identification of an effect specific to the SDR peg.

detail.abstract: Two-leg perpetual positions are often evaluated by matching quote-currency notionals and extrapolating a displayed funding-rate spread. That practice can leave residual quantity, omit eligible funding events, double-count execution costs, and turn unavailable evidence into zero. This methods note develops an event-time ledger for linear, same-settlement-currency perpetual pairs. It combines common-base-quantity closure, four depth-walked fills, per-event funding eligibility, a closed-position identity, a basis-minus-crossing decomposition, scenario-consistent error attribution, and explicit evidence labels. Deterministic examples show that symmetric enumeration produces 7.20 USDT rather than 0.20 USDT in an eight-hour toy window and that a direction-fixed “oracle” need not be an upper bound. A bounded illustration using three routes and two mutually exclusive arms on one day yields net-before-funding paper results from −24.93 to −89.91 USDT. These are not independent trades or portfolio returns. Official settlement marks, account fee evidence, and real orders are absent; exact account net remains unavailable. The framework separates accounting validity from statistical or economic validation.

detail.abstract: Cross-venue funding-carry rankings compare noisy current scenarios, and selecting the maximum can change the relevant error distribution. detail.abstract: Airlines serve meals on most long flights, and from time to time a meal makes passengers ill. Outbreaks on aircraft have affected hundreds of passengers on a single flight and caused deaths. Yet no reported judgment appears to have decided whether illness caused by contaminated food served on board is an "accident" within Article 17 of the Montreal Convention 1999, on which the carrier's liability for bodily injury depends. The claims are usually settled, or fought on the facts, and the question of principle has been left open. This article answers it. Applying the meaning of "accident" established in Air France v. Saks, which is the same in every contracting State, it argues that the service to a passenger of food that is contaminated is an unexpected or unusual event external to the passenger, and so an accident. The objections that the contamination occurred on the ground, that the illness appears after landing, that food poisoning resembles an allergic reaction, and that food is not an aviation risk are each answered. The real difficulties lie elsewhere: in proving bodily injury and causation. The article then considers the carrier's position above the first-tier limit. A caterer that the carrier uses to provide its meal service is its servant or agent, so the carrier can rarely escape liability by blaming it. The defence that the damage was solely due to a third party remains available only against a supplier further up the chain. The article ends with practical guidance on evidence for those who bring and defend these claims.

detail.abstract: The Montreal Convention 1999 makes the carrier answer for the negligence of its servants and agents, and it lets those servants and agents share the carrier's limits of liability. It does not say who they are. The question matters most when a passenger is injured by someone who is not the carrier's employee: a ground handler, a caterer, a maintenance organisation, an airport's contractor. In Mather v. easyJet the Court of Session held that a company appointed by Hamburg Airport to assist passengers with reduced mobility was easyJet's agent, because its services were provided in furtherance of the contract of carriage. easyJet therefore could not treat the company as a third party, and it was liable without limit. This article argues that the court was right about the method and wrong about the result. The words "servant or agent" are treaty terms. They bear an autonomous meaning, drawn from the Convention itself and not from any domestic law of agency. That meaning appears from the history of the words in both authentic languages and from the symmetry between Articles 21 and 30. It appears too from the room the Convention leaves for third parties, from the purpose of Article 30, and from the decisions of the courts of the contracting States. On that meaning, the carrier's servants and agents are the persons it uses, with its consent, to perform the carriage or its obligations under the contract of carriage, and over whose work it has at least some possibility of influence. They do not include a person who discharges its own duty, imposed by law in the general interest of air navigation or the airport. The assistance company in Mather discharged the airport's own statutory duty. It was a third party.

detail.abstract: Widespread narratives portray shea, a tree-based indigenous resource, as "women's gold." Yet, limited qualitative literature exists on how shea activities translate into substantial economic returns. This study examines the labour conditions, income, embodied risks, and purchasing power associated with shea work through semi-structured interviews and participant observation with shea fruit collectors and key informants. Results demonstrate that women spend long and hazardous hours walking to collect fruits and engage in labour-intensive kernel processing activities but earn limited income. This income, however, contributes primarily to short-term household survival with limited purchasing power. Women also faced significant embodied risks, including physical exhaustion, snakebites, skin irritation, and fears of sexual violence in remote fruit collection areas. The study argues that dominant narratives surrounding shea obscures the hidden labour, socio-ecological costs, and unequal income shaping women's participation in the shea sector, particularly among shea fruit collectors. By emphasising labour time, embodied vulnerability, and purchasing power, the article contributes to scholarship on gendered labour and natural resource economies. The study recommends interventions that address fair pricing and labour protection mechanisms, market access, stronger regulation, and the recognition of women's underpaid and unsafe labour within the Shea sector.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the magnitude, timing and stability of exchange rate pass-through in the Democratic Republic of Congo using weekly data from September 2018 to September 2026. The analysis covers official and parallel exchange rates, headline consumer prices, twelve expenditure categories, and constructed non-food and broad-exclusion core aggregates. Asymmetric local projections estimate cumulative price responses, while complementary NARDL specifications reassess long-run relationships and conditional identification exercises examine sensitivity to contemporaneous restrictions. International oil and cereal prices enter as controls. The results indicate substantial transmission extending beyond food prices. In the baseline specifications, a depreciation of approximately 1% is associated with twenty-six-week headline price increases of 0.84% using the official mean exchange rate and 1.26% using the parallel mean. Corresponding appreciation estimates imply declines of 0.84% and 0.42%. However, evidence of directional asymmetry is selective after multiple-testing adjustment, and appreciation responses are sensitive to sample composition and to the late-2025 episode. Within the data construction used here, the NARDL reassessment does not deliver long-run elasticities that pass all diagnostic screens, so long-run inference remains specificationdependent, while causal interpretations remain conditional on timing and exogeneity assumptions. The findings establish the economic relevance of exchange rate transmission without supporting a universal rule of slower appreciation pass-through. They motivate incorporating market-specific and component-level information into inflation forecasting, liquidity assessment and monetary policy communication, while distinguishing the transmission role of the exchange rate from the choice of an exchange rate target.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how mail voting reshapes the political behavior of couples in the United States. Leveraging differences in implementation across states, I study its effects throughout the political decision-making process, both across and within election cycles. Partners overwhelmingly adopt mail voting jointly, reshaping the household's political life: exploiting the varying length of mail-voting periods across states, I show that couple members report significantly more political interactions during such periods, while singles do not. I then document three direct downstream consequences. The introduction of mail voting is associated with a leftward shift among married men, in both partisan ideology and policy views. This effect is primarily concentrated among independent and left-leaning men, while no effects are uncovered among Republicans. Using administrative data on the content and origin of actual ballots, I show that mail voting is associated with significant excess pairs of identical ballots within precincts, suggesting important coordination between partners. Finally, mail-voting periods are associated with a 1.8% increase in the daily number of reported violent incidents between partners, highlighting that increased observability can result in higher within-couple conflict.

detail.abstract: The computational advantage of a graphics processing unit (GPU) does not necessarily translate into a cost advantage. A rented NVIDIA H100 costs less per run than a cloud central processing unit (CPU) only when its measured speedup exceeds the ratio of their hourly prices. That speedup depends on the size and shape of the job and the work surrounding the solver, while the price ratio depends on the cloud provider. We examine this tradeoff using two common financial workloads, measured on an H100 and a Google Cloud machine with 24 virtual CPUs (vCPUs). For parametric value-at-risk (VaR), the H100 was 5 to 30 times faster and cheaper in every case at vast.ai's rental price. At Google Cloud's spot prices for both machines, however, the CPU was cheaper for client portfolios with many positions. For mean-conditional value-at-risk (Mean-CVaR) portfolio optimization, model preparation through CVXPY consumed 70% to 80% of the H100's runtime, limiting its speedup to 2 to 6 times. Constructing the solver matrices directly increased the speedup to 4.6 to 13.6 times. Even with this improvement, the two machines had comparable estimated costs at Google's spot prices across 2,000 to 256,000 scenarios, a range that includes NVIDIA's own example. The Google Cloud cost comparisons use execution times measured on vast.ai and published Google Cloud prices. These results help quantitative developers and computing-budget managers determine when GPU acceleration reduces computing costs. They also help GPU makers and rental providers identify workloads for which the H100 offers an economic advantage. Our four-step method allows both groups to estimate the cost crossover for their own workloads.

detail.abstract: Mobile lending applications have expanded access to credit by reducing the time, geographical and administrative barriers associated with conventional lending. However, the interfaces through which digital credit is marketed and obtained may also shape borrowing decisions through urgency prompts, asymmetric choice architecture, fragmented price disclosures, repeated rollover offers and intrusive requests for personal data. This chapter examines whether Uganda's consumer protection, data protection, financial regulation and competition frameworks adequately address such practices. Using doctrinal analysis and comparative legal inquiry, it evaluates Uganda's existing regulatory framework against selected developments in Ghana and the European Union. It develops a context-sensitive typology of potentially manipulative interface practices and distinguishes legitimate commercial persuasion from design that materially impairs informed and voluntary decision-making. The chapter further considers how algorithmic personalisation and emerging agentic artificial intelligence complicate regulatory approaches centred on disclosure, consent and identifiable human intention. It argues that meaningful consumer protection requires more than improved disclosure: it requires scrutiny of how digital credit choices are presented, personalised and executed. The chapter proposes proportionate interface fairness duties, risk-based audits, meaningful consent and exit mechanisms, regulatory experimentation and accessible remedies.

detail.abstract: Predictive policing systems forecast where recorded crime will occur. Governing them requires knowing how much of a forecast is new information and how much is a stable geography that any method would reproduce. I study monthly recorded crime in Chicago's 77 community areas from 2015 to 2025 (2.76 million records). It is concentrated and stable: the ten highest areas hold 34% of records with 22% of residents, and rankings for 2015 to 2019 and 2021 to 2025 correlate at 0.99. Across four rolling forecast origins, a seasonal ARIMA beats seasonal naive and plain ARIMA benchmarks (median error 11.9%), yet its ranking finds no more of the ten highest areas than last year's totals (8.75 against 9). In a spatial error model, one standard deviation more low-income households goes with rates about 34% higher. Recorded crime reflects reporting and police activity, so I make no claim about bias or causes.

detail.abstract: Understanding international trade shocks is key to fostering global trade resilience, but complex supply chains and geopolitical dynamics make predicting disruptions difficult. Rather than forecasting specific events, this study uses directed, weighted wheat trade networks from the BACI-CEPII database to introduce a hazard-agnostic, product-level model for characterizing and improving national exposure to import shocks. Our network-based measure of trade diversity captures the correlation structure of risks across suppliers by grouping them into geographic "distance bins." Diversity is calculated over this structure and used to model the annual probability of shock exceedance in historical wheat trade time series. In our dataset of 152 nations, geographically diverse import networks experienced less frequent and severe import disruptions. We also examine alternative network configurations for Egypt to demonstrate the method's utility in mitigating identified risks. This framework, paired with scenario analysis, can help identify strategies and set measurable targets to achieve trade resilience goals.

detail.abstract: At the final stage of the Second World War, Romania was occupied by the Red Army. Soviet officials imposed a government dominated by communists although this political formation was not very popular in Romania. In the next years, the country's political system was gradually transformed and in December 1947 the Romanian People's Republic was proclaimed. A complex power struggle started among the Romanian communists and ended with the victory of Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej. Meanwhile, the national economy experienced a transition to a Stalinist model. After Stalin's death, in March 1953, his successors implemented some reforms meant to solve the problems of the Soviet economy. Between 1953 and 1960, these changes were either quickly imitated by Romanian authorities or, at least, praised in the media. From 1961 to 1964, Gheorghiu-Dej, whose position in Romania had strengthened, decided to ignore or even to oppose some economic reforms from Soviet Union. His successor, Nicolae Ceauşescu, initiated, in 1960s and 1970s, his own reforms meant to increase the efficiency of the Romanian economy. Some of such measures had some similarities with the reforms proposed in these times, by Alexei Kosygin. Instead, the Perestroika, launched in 1985 by Mikhail Gorbachev met Ceausescu's opposition.

detail.abstract: Standard valuation treats a housing shock as a level effect that is capitalized locally and, at most, smoothed outward by diffusion. The strongest recent econophysical evidence is consistent with exactly this diffusive picture: the spatial structure of observed price fields decays logarithmically, the signature of a twodimensional random-diffusion process rather than of a traveling wave. We take that evidence as the null. Urban Wave Theory (UWT) asks a narrower and testable question on top of it: under what conditions does a shock propagate as a finite-speed front rather than spread parabolically? We write a single classical state variable, the log-price-deviation field, and let it obey one damped nonlinear wave equation on an anisotropic network (conduit) metric of the city. Linear diffusion and a screened steady state emerge as the overdamped limit; a finite-speed front emerges as the underdamped limit. A dimensionless propagation number separates the two. The contribution is a falsifiable criterion: a wave is claimed only if first-passage times scale linearly with conduit distance, the steady response is exponentially screened with an estimable attenuation length, the propagation number exceeds unity, and the recovered speed is stable across independent shocks. Because a finite front speed can also be produced by nonlinear reaction-diffusion, we require the underdamped (oscillatory) signature in addition to the arrival-time scaling, and we demonstrate numerically that the criterion declines to admit a wave in a reaction-diffusion front. The only element borrowed from quantum theory is a bounded interference term in decision weights during announcement windows, taken from quantum decision theory and deliberately confined to that layer; the field itself remains classical. We state this interference effect as a hypothesis with a parameter-free qualitative prediction, and we set out an identification strategy for the underlying inverse problem. The framework subsumes hedonic, repeat-sales, and spatial-econometric estimands as functionals of one field and yields a small number of estimands, a front speed, an attenuation length, and an interference premium, which existing methods do not.

detail.abstract: The European Central Bank and the Reserve Bank of Australia have raised interest rates through 2026 while inflation has risen. We show why, by sorting each consumer price by who sets it rather than by what households buy. In the euro area, rebuilt from 293 classes in 21 member states, prices set by governments, regulators and institutions hold 0.33 of the 0.52-point core excess over target in the year to September 2026, and German government-set prices and Spanish domestic businesses’ prices make up three-fifths of it; French and Italian domestic prices are already below target. In Australia the same prices hold 0.44 of the 1.03-point excess in the monthly trimmed mean, twelve months to September 2026, measured with monthly changes added. In local projections on each central bank’s own policy surprises, a tightening reaches customers, lowering spending, building, output or jobs, but no group of prices set by governments, regulators, institutions or domestic businesses falls clearly within two years. Set prediction by prediction, the orthodox step fails or finds no support wherever the two readings differ, and the reading by who sets the price holds wherever it makes a claim, including four calls on Australia’s September 2026 figures lodged the day before release. The results follow from a condition standard models leave unstated. They compute outcomes from decisions and assume the decisions are carried out, the case S = 1 of Y = d(P) × S; where that holds their results hold, and where it does not a match with the outturn is luck. We answer thirteen objections, including that transmission economics already handles this, and lodge six euro-area calls before the data that decide them.

detail.abstract: Afghanistan's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2016 marked a significant step towards integrating its economy into the multilateral trading system after decades of conflict and economic disruption. Membership created opportunities for improved market access, participation in trade negotiations, and reform of domestic legislation in accordance with WTO agreements. Nevertheless, questions concerning formal membership, representation, and effective participation raise important legal issues. This article examines Afghanistan's accession, the WTO's institutional framework, and the legal implications of any alleged suspension, abeyance, restriction of representation, or expulsion. It analyses the Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the WTO, Afghanistan's accession commitments, and the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS), particularly its implications for Afghanistan's trademark legislation. The article distinguishes suspension, abeyance, withdrawal, and expulsion as separate legal concepts with different consequences. Official WTO records continue to identify Afghanistan as a Member since 29 July 2016, with its accession protocol listed as in force. Therefore, any claim of formal suspension requires authoritative legal evidence. Using a doctrinal legal methodology, the article evaluates relevant treaty provisions, institutional procedures, continuing obligations, and potential remedies. It concludes by recommending legal clarification, appropriate institutional engagement, diplomatic dialogue, and domestic legislative reform to protect Afghanistan's trade interests and strengthen compliance with its WTO commitments.

detail.abstract: The daily change in aggregate dealer gamma exposure explains same-day S&P 500 returns far better than the level of that exposure. Using 3,909 trading days from 2 May 2011 to 13 November 2026, a regression of the daily index return on the change in the SqueezeMetrics GEX index ("gamma positioning momentum") has an R 2 of 17.6%, against 6.9% for price normalised GEX and 0.1% for its one-day lag. The sign of the GEX change matches the sign of the return on 80.5% of days. Days in the top quintile of GEX changes return +0.92% on average; days in the bottom quintile return-0.82%. Momentum dominates the level in every calendar year and in every rolling one-year window, with a median one-year R 2 of 41.8%. The relationship is contemporaneous, not predictive. Today's GEX change has no power for tomorrow's return on its own (t =-0.49). Most of its explanatory power is shared with the same-day change in the VIX, and adding it to a VIX regression raises R^2 from 65.5% to 67.6%. The level carries a different kind of information: it predicts next-day absolute returns (R^2 of 10.9%) but not their direction. We find no evidence that GEX and the index level are cointegrated, so an error-correction interpretation is not supported. We read the results as a decomposition: the level of dealer gamma describes the volatility regime, while its daily change co-moves with the direction of returns, partly by construction.

detail.abstract: Nearly a century after Ramsey (1928), Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) models remain the backbone of modern macroeconomics, yet their dynamic and empirical analysis still relies pervasively on first-order linearization around the balanced growth path. In this paper, we argue that whilst linearization is mathematically unavoidable for local Blanchard-Kahn saddle-path stability analysis, extrapolating it to impulse response functions and historical shock extraction introduces severe distortions. Using an 18-dimensional monetary-fiscal endogenous growth model with human capital and banking frictions, we contrast linearized state-space dynamics against an exact nonlinear Fair-Taylor shooting solver and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) policy approximator. We show that linear mappings enforce false symmetry, strict proportionality, and state-independence. Moreover, across U.S. historical data (1920-2004), linear pseudoinverse extraction yields economically impossible realizations-including negative banking productivity and credit flows-beyond the nonlinear saddle-path boundary, whereas the Ramsey PINN strictly preserves structural feasibility.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the macroeconomic determinants of the Ethiopian insurance sector and the direction of its causal linkage with economic growth over the fiscal years 2017–2025. Industry aggregates compiled from the audited financials of the Association of Ethiopian Insurers are matched year-by-year with macroeconomic series from the statistical annexes of the National Bank of Ethiopia, and the resulting nine-observation annual panel is analysed within a parsimonious trivariate vector autoregression (VAR) in industry gross written premium (IGWP) growth, real GDP growth and CPI inflation, complemented by Johansen cointegration analysis, Granger causality and block exogeneity tests, orthogonalised impulse responses and forecast error variance decompositions. Descriptively, the industry nearly quadrupled nominal premiums (a compound annual growth rate of 18.11 percent) and expanded its balance sheet more than fivefold, yet insurance penetration halved from 0.591 percent to 0.272 percent of GDP because nominal GDP grew twice as fast amid a double-digit inflation regime that peaked at 33.8 percent in 2021/22. Econometrically, log premiums are integrated of order one, and nominal premiums share a single long-run relationship with broad money. The VAR delivers the positive sign pattern predicted by the demand-following hypothesis, but neither real GDP growth nor inflation attains conventional significance in the premium growth equation (joint block test p = 0.475). The supply-leading hypothesis finds no support: premium growth does not Granger-cause real GDP growth (p = 0.146), the impulse response of output to a premium shock is not positive at any horizon, and premium shocks explain less than 6 percent of the forecast error variance of growth, whereas macroeconomic shocks, led by inflation, account for roughly 42 percent of four-year-ahead premium uncertainty. The sector is accordingly characterised as demand-following with weak statistical visibility, and the policy conclusions anchor on disinflation, growth-linked demand expansion and the integration of insurance statistics into macroprudential surveillance.

detail.abstract: Firms invest heavily in reducing the volatility of their real output. To establish this fact, I introduce a new measure of this investment: total salaries paid to supply chain risk management (SCRM) workers. SCRM investment is strongly predictive of lower output volatility within industry and is large in the aggregate, approximately $60-$130 billion annually among US nonfinancial firms. High-SCRM firms have more diversified supplier networks and are significantly less likely to lose a major customer following industry-wide supply shocks relative to low-SCRM industry peers. Despite its benefits, investment in SCRM is restricted by financial constraints for many firms. Using a novel IV for IPO completion---SEC office workload at the time of filing---I show that IPO completion causes compliers to nearly double their SCRM wage bill allocation post-IPO, an effect driven by small firms expecting large cash proceeds from the equity sale. SCRM, by reducing output volatility, appears to contribute to firm value through a channel distinct from its role in reducing cash flow volatility: ability to reliably deliver on customer contracts. I develop a model in which SCRM investment reduces the probability of an output shortfall, which increases firm value in a way that cannot be replicated by financial instruments. The model's core prediction is that whether SCRM and financial hedging are close substitutes depends on the cost of losing a customer; this prediction holds in the data.

detail.abstract: We show how investors' local bias shapes both the demand for mutual funds and their supply. We identify investor locations using the in-state tax advantage of single-state municipal funds. Funds offered by families located in their investors' states are more than twice as large as funds offered by out-of-state families and attract significantly higher annual flows. Fees, maturity, credit quality, and returns do not explain the size differential, which is largest in direct-sold share classes, consistent with familiarity rather than an information advantage or local distribution networks. Supply mirrors this demand: families are far more likely to offer funds for their home state and offer more of them there across a broader range of product types. Families that sell directly to investors serve fewer states than those that sell through brokers, suggesting that intermediated distribution partly substitutes for familiarity. Beyond municipal funds, self-directed households at a large discount brokerage are more likely to hold mutual funds offered by nearby families. Finally, the growth rate of fund families from new entrants in a metropolitan area increases with its population and decreases with its number of existing families, consistent with local demand driving the geographic diffusion of the fund industry over the past century.

detail.abstract: Technological revolutions depend not only on advances in knowledge, capital investment, and institutional conditions but also, at certain stages, on the innovation functions of key entrepreneurs. This paper develops a conditional framework for examining how political measures directed at an entrepreneur may affect technological realization through disruptions to judgment, coordination, risk-bearing, and industrial networks. It distinguishes ex ante structural dependence from effective non-substitutability within a relevant innovation window and separates the entrepreneur-mediated channel from parallel regulatory, market, and financial effects. The framework identifies three distinct potential consequences. At the firm level, failure of timely internal substitution and late restoration of entrepreneurial functions may cause an irreversible opportunity loss (Proposition 2a). At the social level, the loss may propagate into persistent lock-in of a technological path under additional conditions (Proposition 2b-L). Alternatively, society may receive an economically equivalent technological service later, including in cases in which the firm ultimately preserves its own opportunity (Proposition 2b-D). The delay branch distinguishes the pre-intervention forecast of first supply from independently estimated no-intervention counterfactual and observed dates. A positive realization-time difference does not, by itself, establish a negative net social-welfare effect. The paper specifies falsifiable conditions and identification requirements without claiming completed causal estimation or a uniformly adverse impact of political intervention.

detail.abstract: Classical competition law has been built on price-effect analysis and the model of productmarket rivalry, and struggles to apprehend the distinctive structure of digital markets. When dominance manifests not through above-cost pricing but through ecosystem enclosure, information asymmetry, visibility and traditional ex-post framework enforcement arrives too late and looks in the wrong direction. This paper traces a structural transition from the retrospective competition law towards an ex-ante approach designed specifically to govern growing digital markets before harm emerges. Indian Digital Competition Bill, 2024, introduced by the Committee for Digital Competition Law under the guidance of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and the European Digital Market Act, 2022, represent parallel but distant responses to this challenge. The paper argues that both marked a significant shift from the classical regime; the Indian draft remains incomplete without fully interrogating the nature of the power of those intermediate exercises. The paper advances towards a reconceptualization of digital dominance as informational and instructional power rather than merely economic strength. It contends that meaningful regulation of digital markets requires a foundational shift away from price-effects analysis towards an inquiry into platform-mediated markets, the ecosystem dependence of businesses, control over information visibility, and information asymmetry between the platform and individuals who rely on it.

detail.abstract: How did Congolese firms and banks invest and extend credit when commercial outlets, prices or financing conditions became hard to predict? detail.abstract: This paper studies the demand for money on the territory of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo, from the creation of the Bank of the Belgian Congo in 1909 to 1980. Colonial archives make it possible to trace the composition of money holdings from 1910 and to relate the money stock to GDP for 1953 and 1954, for the Belgian Congo and Ruanda-Urundi combined. For the post-independence period, we estimate the short-run relationship between real money balances, economic activity and the previous year’s inflation. Over the common period 1964–1980, a 1% rise in real GDP is associated with an estimated increase of 1.18% in real M1 balances and 1.07% in real M2 balances. The 95% confidence interval includes zero for M2. When the M1 sample starts in 1961, its income coefficient falls to 0.22. The effect of past inflation remains imprecise, and stability tests give divergent conclusions around 1976. Finally, the demonetisation of December 1979 reveals a measurement difficulty that is decisive for historical interpretation. Between 1979 and 1980, M2 velocity falls when calculated on the December stock but rises when the average of two successive December stocks is used.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the evolution of prices on the territory of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo, from the first colonial cost-of-living benchmarks to the end of the 1970s. The institutional chronology begins in 1909. The price observations used go back to 1935, and the macroeconomic analysis covers 21 annual rates, from 1960 to 1980. In the retrospective series of the Central Bank of the Congo (BCC), inflation averages 19.2% a year between 1960 and 1975, then 69.2% between 1976 and 1980. The Kinshasa archives show how much this rise differed by place of purchase. In 1979, annual-average food prices rose by 154.9% in shops and by 96.8% in markets. The annual estimates are also sensitive to the historical breakdown of the sample. The coefficient on lagged inflation, estimated at 0.48 over 1961–1980, becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero once the shift in the mean level from 1976 is taken into account. In this short sample, the apparent persistence of inflation therefore partly reflects the clustering of several years of rapid price increases. The paper documents this acceleration and its spread across categories of goods, while setting out the limits of attributing it to monetary, fiscal and external factors.

detail.abstract: Many journals now restrict the use of AI in writing. Rules that punish openly disclosed AI use are meant to protect honesty. This note examines what such rules do to one kind of writer: a person who has a real idea but cannot write a publishable text alone, because of limited English, limited time, or limited ability to draft for long hours. Using the theory of Cornered Rational Choice, I argue that for this writer, writing alone is not a real option. If that is so, a higher penalty on disclosed AI use cannot send the writer back to writing alone. For writers who remain in the publication process, it may shift behavior from open to hidden AI use. The note explains the idea in plain words, uses a small choice model to show it, and states four hypotheses for later testing. It is a theoretical argument and presents no new data. It does not defend hiding AI use, false references, or handing responsibility to a machine, but instead focuses on whether the tool used to make a text should decide its fate or whether the text should be judged by its ideas and evidence.

detail.abstract: This working paper extends the history of the Congolese financial system studied from 1909 to 1980 (Pinshi, 2026a). Drawing on the reports of the Bank of Zaire, the Central Bank of the Congo (BCC) and IMF statistics, it reconstructs the evolution of credit, deposits and capital flows from 1980 to 2010. Two prolonged contractions frame the crisis of the 1990s. Real GDP fell by 37.2% between 1988 and 1994, then by 19.8% between 1995 and 2001, after a brief rebound in 1995. Interest rate and foreign exchange market liberalisation came in 2001, while activity was still declining. Between 2001 and 2010, credit to the private sector rose from 0.77% to 6.57% of GDP using the denominators published at the time. With identical stocks, retrospective GDP figures give 0.46% and 4.01% respectively. The recovery of credit appears in both series and was accompanied by high dollarisation: in 2010, foreign currencies accounted for 84.8% of deposits. The external accounts shed light on another dimension of this trajectory. From 2001, the direct investment balance was positive, while the combined balance of direct, portfolio and other investment was negative. The chronology thus makes it possible to distinguish three developments whose timing and magnitude differ: financial opening, the recovery of bank credit and the external financing of the economy.

detail.abstract: Agriculture in Bangladesh has a significant impact on the economy, contributing 11.37 percent to the national GDP and employing almost 45 percent of the total labor force. Both climatic and non-climatic factors significantly influence the Agricultural productivity in Bangladesh, as the country is highly climate sensitive due to its geographical location. Climate factors (rainfall, Temperature, CO₂ emissions) and non-climate inputs (fertilizer) critically influence agricultural productivity, yet their combined short-and long-term macroeconomic impacts remain underexplored. This study examines the effects of climatic and non-climatic factors on agricultural productivity and their subsequent macroeconomic implications in Bangladesh. Using time series data (1990-2021), we employ the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to assess long-term elasticities and the Granger causality test to determine directional relationships between variables The ARDL results reveal significant longterm elasticities: a 1% increase in fertilizer use raises agricultural output by 0.49%, while a 1% rise in Temperature reduces output by 0.04%. CO₂ emissions and rainfall show positive impacts (0.71% and 0.96%, respectively). The error correction term (-0.49) indicates the system corrects 49% of short-run disequilibrium annually. Granger causality confirms bidirectional relationships between fertilizer use and agricultural productivity (F-stat = 3.72), while Temperature unidirectionally affects output (F-stat = 4.22). The findings validate that non-climate factors (fertilizer) and climate variables (CO₂, rainfall) positively influence agricultural output, whereas Temperature exerts adverse effects. These results align with prior regional studies but highlight Bangladesh's unique susceptibility to temperature fluctuations.

detail.abstract:
How did the central bank’s ability to influence the cost of credit evolve in Zaire, and then in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, between 1980 and 2010? This study extends the history of Congolese monetary policy traced for 1909–1980 (Pinshi, 2026b). It brings together the decisions recorded in the central bank’s reports with 31 annual observations on money, prices, the exchange rate and credit, and with 240 monthly interest rate observations. Three decisions mark the transformation of instruments: the abolition of direct credit controls in 1993, the liberalisation of bank rates and the floating of the franc in 2001, and the introduction of the Central Bank of the Congo (BCC) bill in 2002.

Over the whole period, broad money growth is closely associated with annual inflation, including when 1993 and 1994 are removed from the estimation. At monthly frequency, between 2002 and 2010, a one-percentage-point rise in the policy rate is associated, in the same month, with a rise of 0.83 point in the lending rate and 0.27 point in the deposit rate in domestic currency. The scope of this transmission nevertheless depends on the weight of credit in the economy. Relative to archival GDP, credit to enterprises and households, then to the private sector depending on the nomenclature, fell from 5.84% in 1980 to 0.77% in 2001, before rising to 6.57% in 2010. The estimates thus document a transmission of the policy rate to domestic-currency banking conditions, whose causal effect on prices remains to be established.

This paper analyses the methodological shift triggered by the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in economic modelling and forecasting. The study identifies the key prospects and threats associated with this transformation and shows that AI opens up new opportunities for the rapid analysis of big data, the detection of complex non-linear relationships, and stronger microfoundations of existing models. At the same time, its implementation gives rise to fundamental challenges, including the problem of interpretability, the risk of self-fulfilling forecasts, and new classes of cyber threats. The main conclusion of the paper is that the principal danger of applying AI lies in a change in the epistemological foundations of economics, leading to the substitution of predictive accuracy for explanatory power. As a response, the paper substantiates the concept of "hybrid intelligence", which requires a synergy between economic theory and AI algorithms, and formulates practical steps for its implementation, including the development of explainable AI (XAI) standards, the formation of ethical norms, and the transformation of economics education.

The paper was presented at the International Scientific and Practical Conference "Asset Management – 2025: Artificial Intelligence in Economic Decision-Making: Assets, Actors, Strategies" (MGIMO University, Moscow, 9 December 2025).

detail.abstract: When a tariff is abolished, an underwriter types the rate. How consistent are those rates? Using 166,542 fire policies of one Iranian insurer, we show that an audit of administrative records must first separate three things a vignette study never meets. A naive audit finds a log-rate standard deviation of 0.17 (about 17 percent) in the same city and month. But 83 percent of the book is residential business priced by product rules; one bulk agreement produces half of the remaining dispersion; and 73 percent of residential policies were issued in batches, so policies are not decisions. Among pricing decisions on identically recorded risks, two decisions in one city and month carry the same rate 88 percent of the time in commercial lines. Agreement is 88 percent at renewal and 59 percent between unrelated accounts. Dispersion is persistent, not random. Lacking losses and underwriter identities, we document dispersion, not error.

detail.abstract: When monetary tightening turns central bank results negative, the cost falls on the government, but the deduction central banks place before their transfers decides when it reaches the budget. I code who sets this deduction at 55 central banks and how each loss of 2008-15 and 2022-24 was absorbed. The bank sets it alone at 33 and with the government at ten more; where a bank's buffer could cover a loss, banks other than the Swiss National Bank released it in 42 of 47 cases. Of the Eurosystem's losses of 2022-24, equal to 1% of euro-area GDP, 60% was absorbed by buffers withheld in earlier years, 36% was carried forward and 4% was met from public funds. The rule re-times the fiscal cost of tightening rather than changing it. In a New Keynesian model calibrated to the Bundesbank, a Treasury that covers losses at once contracts the budget by 1% of GDP during the tightening and lowers the peak policy rate by 14 basis points; buffers spread the cost over a decade. Coverage is never far from the best rule, so the case for buffers rests on independence, which independence indices do not record.

detail.abstract: Proactive care offers opportunities to improve long-term outcomes for patients with chronic conditions, yet its delivery requires additional medical resources such as nursing time, monitoring infrastructure, and clinical review capacity. Thus, allocating limited proactive-care capacity among patient population is a critical operational challenge, requiring care managers to repeatedly decide whom to serve, when, and with which intervention. These decisions are further complicated by evolving incompletely observed health conditions. Motivated by these challenges, we develop a dynamic resource allocation model and an efficient dynamic programming algorithm that account for the long-term effects of interventions on both patient health and the information available for subsequent decisions, guiding care allocation to improve population health under intervention-specific capacity constraints. Our analysis establishes theoretical guarantees for computational accuracy and allocation performance under appropriate regularity conditions. We apply the approach to nurse telephone support and home telemonitoring in chronic heart failure management through simulations using a published clinical model calibrated to randomized clinical trial data. Across the scenarios examined, our policy achieves approximately 4%-10% higher average health returns than other tested policies under the same capacities. It also yields approximately 2.8 additional months of cumulative survival per patient, together with lower mortality and a larger share of the original cohort in less severe disease states. This application illustrates how our approach translates clinically estimated disease dynamics and intervention effects into capacity-feasible care assignments, providing a basis for decision support with the potential to improve both survival and population health through better allocation of existing services.

detail.abstract: Walk down your school hallways at 7:15 AM and it's obvious: teens are exhausted. But here's the weird part-two kids can scroll on their phones in bed for two hours, yet one shows up functioning while the other looks like zombies. We know blue light chokes off melatonin production. That's basic biology. What nobody can agree on is why the damage is so uneven. Is it just a lack of self-control, or is it literally written in our DNA? Ever since the first ever paper on the effects of circadian rhythms caused by social media had been released in 2017, in the University of Pittsburgh preventive medicine journal by J.C. Levenson et al. Since then, there have been countless discoveries and theses released on this pressing issue. We spent months digging into PubMed to see if clock genes (PER3, CLOCK) and dopamine reward genes (DRD2, ANKK1) explain this gap. Throw in pubertal clock delays, and teens are basically stuck in a biological deadlock. We aren't lab scientists generating fresh petri-dish data-we are high schoolers trying to connect four scientific fields that rarely align with each other, looking at the evidence with fresh eyes, and calling out the bad science where we see it.

detail.abstract: Between 2012 and 2025 the United States and the Central Bank of Iraq barred 33 Iraqi banks from the dollar: 46 percent of all licenses, half the private banks, about a tenth of banking assets; the 22 banks the Union of Arab Banks counted as barred in spring 2024 had carried about a third of the dollars the window sold. This paper builds the first dated series of those restrictions and asks what they did to bank intermediation. The answer, in the aggregates: less than either side claims. The bundled shock of November 2022, the electronic screening platform together with bans on the four banks that carried 40 percent of window flow, raised excess reserves about 20 percent and cut the money multiplier 4.6 percent on impact; the later bans show only transitory hoarding, gone within eighteen months, with the Central Bank's own policy rate explaining the parking thereafter. The aggregates bound, rather than measure, losses inside the restricted banks, which hold about 2 percent of deposits. The multiplier never exceeded 1.47 because the banks were never lenders: in 2012 to 2017 the window rent pool ran 1.06 to 1.76 times the system's entire potential net interest income, and the window banks' own accounts show 68 to 83 percent of operating income from commissions and currency, not loans. A counterfactual in the author's structural model prices the ban-era hoard at 0.3 to 2.8 percent of one year's GDP, against about 7.5 percent of GDP forgone in every year that the counter, rather than a lending system, allocates the deposits.

detail.abstract: Using monthly securities-lending data for Hong Kong-listed equities from 2013 to 2025, I test whether the average loan fee predicts the cross-section of stock returns outside the United States. Stocks with higher fees earn lower subsequent returns. The monthly rank information coefficient is-0.058 (Newey-West t =-6.4), and a long-short portfolio that buys the lowest-fee decile and sells the highest-fee decile earns 1.46% per month (t = 4.6) equal-weighted and 1.64% (t = 4.0) value-weighted, with a three-factor alpha of 1.14% (t = 3.8). detail.abstract: Public discourse surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly bifurcated into two dominant narratives. The first emphasises speculative excess, framing contemporary AI capital markets as an analogue to the late-1990s Dot-com Bubble. The second foregrounds socio-technical anxieties concerning labour displacement, epistemic pollution, and regulatory containment. While both perspectives capture salient empirical phenomena, they risk obscuring a deeper structural transformation. Drawing upon evolutionary economics, institutional theory, and emerging frameworks on autonomous civilisation and Quantum Gadaa, this paper argues that financial speculation and technological paradigms are analytically distinct phenomena. Just as the collapse of speculative equity valuations during the Dot-com crash did not arrest the underlying Internet Revolution, cyclical volatility in AI markets will not forestall the transition toward an autonomous civilisation defined by unprecedented knowledge abundance. Consequently, contemporary society confronts an institutional deficit rather than a technological one. The central governance question is not whether autonomous capabilities should be curtailed, but whether institutional architectures can evolve with sufficient velocity to steward systems capable of scaling knowledge synthesis, cognitive amplification, and planetary problem-solving.

detail.abstract: Block-chain is a revolutionary innovation in the domain of secure info management, decentralized computing and digital communication. Block-chain is essentially based on a set of essential mathematical principles that help assure data integrity, transparency, security and trust among the distributed parties without having to rely on a centralized authority. In this paper, the mathematical concepts that support the work of block-chain technology are discussed and the importance of cryptography, number theory, discrete mathematics, probability theory, graph theory and computational complexity is highlighted. Secure and reliable operations of a block-chain are provided by a set of mathematical tools such as particular attention to cryptographic hash functions, public-key cryptography, digital signatures, Merkle trees and consensus mechanisms. Additionally, the paper explores the role of mathematical algorithms in transaction verification, block validation, network synchronization, and preventing malicious alterations to the blocks. Additionally, the study underscores the importance of mathematical concepts for the decentralization, scalability and fault-tolerance of block-chain networks. This work relates theoretical mathematical concepts with their applications in the block-chain architecture, which will give more depth to the understanding of how mathematics is the base of trust and security in decentralized networks. Through the exploration, it is shown that block-chain is not simply a technological invention, but an implementation of the mathematical theories and computational algorithms which are used to solve real-life problems.

detail.abstract: Europe's economic core is usually treated as a settled fact: a group of countries at the centre of the continent's business cycle. We ask whether that group is also the one through which downturns travel. Using monthly industrial production for 32 European economies from 2000 to 2026, we measure whether a sharp downturn in one country is soon followed by one in another, and we let the data choose the core rather than assuming it. The group that emerges is not the familiar one: it admits Spain and Italy while leaving out France, Belgium and the Netherlands. Two procedures built on different assumptions arrive at the same group. Membership is not the whole story either, since Germany proves more often on the receiving end of its partners' contractions than the source of theirs. Most striking, the core's closer connections do not survive the removal of the financial crisis and the pandemic, even though the great majority of sharp national downturns fall outside those two crises. Being able to name a core is not the same as showing that one persists between crises. Downturns travel within a month, along routes that trade helps explain: a country is most exposed to the partners that buy its exports. The core-centred pattern in good times arrives later and rests largely on the 2020 rebound. The question worth asking is therefore not only who belongs to Europe's core, but when, in which direction, and through which relationships its economies become vulnerable together.

detail.abstract: Recent single-question crowd wisdom algorithms use higher-order beliefs to identify truth, even when the majority is wrong. These algorithms rely on a Bayesian framework where agents observe an informative signal and update on a common prior. The common prior assumption could be restrictive, as it rules out the possibility that rational agents who observe the same evidence might still disagree. People may have different priors due to their background, experience, political alignment etc. This paper investigates the feasibility of crowd wisdom under prior heterogeneity. We establish the linear equivalence property for first and second-order beliefs, which gives a sufficiency condition for prior-invariant crowd wisdom. Three empirical studies illustrate how a decision maker can test linear equivalence in practice, and whether it predicts accuracy. The first study examines survey data from the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament (XPT), which elicited expert and superforecaster beliefs on long-term risks from AI, climate change, nuclear war, and pandemics. The second study examines business managers' inflation expectations, using perceived inflation in the recent past as a proxy for heterogeneous priors. The third study uses probability judgements on general knowledge questions with known correct answers. Results suggest that beliefs do not always satisfy linear equivalence. However, the decision maker can identify if they do so in a given problem. Furthermore, whether the beliefs satify linear equivalence or not predicts the accuracy of crowd wisdom.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. Across all three benchmarks, we found that increasing the thinking effort does not increase decision quality in a statistically meaningful way. The same change in thinking effort raises stated confidence at a statistically significant level, so extra thinking buys confidence rather than correctness. We also measure the calibration of these models (how well their reported confidence percentage matches their true correctness percentage) in these tasks and show that most models are not well-calibrated at every effort level. We also find that errors are strongly shared: when one model errs in a task, several others tend to err on that same task. Furthermore, on tasks where several models all err, a large number of them pick the same wrong product.
